posts.title: Internet poetics
posts.description: One of the three things I spent time on while on research leave earlier this year was exploring intersections between Internet art and Internet research - including through having more regular studio time . So I’m looking forward to continuing to explore this area through co-teaching a much-refreshed module on Internet poetics this coming autumn. 🍂🍵🌌🌕 Alternating between small screen walks and studio sessions, we will explore how features of the internet can be artistically reworked for critical inquiry into digital culture. We’ll also be drawing inspiration from repertoires of the vernacular web , handmade web , poetic web and associated tendencies - to explore how artistic approaches might support collective inquiry , experimentation and imagination around other ways of being online together. posts.title: "Netstalgia Not Acceptable" with Olia Lialina and Winnie Soon at "I Miss the Internet", Photographers’ Gallery, 17th September 2026
posts.description: I’m looking forward to joining Olia Lialina and Winnie Soon for a discussion on “Netstalgia Not Acceptable” at The Photographers’ Gallery on Thursday 17th September 2026. This is part of I Miss the Internet organised with Error 417 Expectation Failed - featuring talks, discussions and performances from Dana Dawud , Lenyx Dickey , Mariana Marangoni , Lola Odelola , Lucia Rebolino and Kat Macdonald ( London Community Laptop Orchestra ). Further details and booking links can be found here . From the event page: “ I miss the internet ” has become a familiar refrain online. Referencing a popular meme , it is nonsensical but evocative: the phrase prompts us to ask what, exactly, “the internet” refers to. What is being mourned is something more elusive: is it the “old internet”, an imagined internet that never fully materialised, or a projection from a future in which today’s internet has already become history? posts.title: Who Makes Public Data? Communities, Cultures and the State - webinar with Aapti Institute on 9th September 2026
posts.description: Looking forward to joining this webinar on “Who Makes Public Data? Communities, Cultures, and the State” organised by Aapti Institute (Bengaluru, India) on Wednesday 9th September 2026. Pallab Deb , Liliana Bounegru , Kumar Sambhav Shrivastava and I will discuss “how data becomes public through the social practices, institutions, infrastructures and communities involved in producing, interpreting, sharing and contesting it” - drawing on Public Data Cultures and the Data Journalism Handbook as well as work with Land Conflict Watch , Nutgraph and the Public Data Lab . Here’s the blurb and registration link: This session explores the social and cultural dimensions of public data: how data is produced, interpreted, shared, contested, and made meaningful through relationships between communities, institutions, and the state.
